scenes.tts: Ectoderm can become skin or nervous system. What decides which one it becomes?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Map and the Question. A sheet of cells splits into two paths, one labeled skin, one labeled nervous system. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Ectoderm can become skin or nervous system. What decides which one it becomes?

scenes.tts: Start with the map. A blastula is the early frog embryo, a hollow ball of cells.
scenes.visual: The blastula map: a hollow ball of cells drawn in cross-section, animal cap at the top shaded as ectoderm, blastocoel inside, endoderm at the floor; beside it a gastrula with the blastopore groove on the lower half, its dorsal lip labeled organizer, dorsal and ventral arrows. Only the blastula is shown at first; label: blastula.
scenes.narration: Start with the map. A blastula is the early frog embryo, a hollow ball of cells.

scenes.tts: Inside is a fluid-filled cavity, the blastocoel. The roof of that cavity is the animal cap.
scenes.visual: The blastocoel fills with pale blue; the roof of cells above it highlights. Label: animal cap.
scenes.narration: Inside is a fluid-filled cavity, the blastocoel. The roof of that cavity is the animal cap.

scenes.tts: The cap is ectoderm, the outer germ layer. It gives rise to both the skin and the nervous system.
scenes.visual: The cap cells glow; two arrows lead from them to icons of skin and of a brain and spinal cord. Label: ectoderm.
scenes.narration: The cap is ectoderm, the outer germ layer. It gives rise to both the skin and the nervous system.

scenes.tts: The outer layer of skin is the epidermis. Keep that word; it is one of the two answers.
scenes.visual: The skin icon enlarges; label: epidermis.
scenes.narration: The outer layer of skin is the epidermis. Keep that word; it is one of the two answers.

scenes.tts: Gastrulation is the set of cell movements that form the germ layers.
scenes.visual: The ball shifts into a gastrula; cells begin to stream inward. Label: gastrulation.
scenes.narration: Gastrulation is the set of cell movements that form the germ layers.

scenes.tts: It begins at the blastopore, a groove on the lower half of the embryo, where cells start to move inside.
scenes.visual: A groove opens on the lower half of the embryo; arrows show cells turning inward there. Label: blastopore.
scenes.narration: It begins at the blastopore, a groove on the lower half of the embryo, where cells start to move inside.

scenes.tts: The tissue at the blastopore's dorsal lip is the organizer.
scenes.visual: The upper edge of the groove lights. Label: dorsal lip, organizer.
scenes.narration: The tissue at the blastopore's dorsal lip is the organizer.

scenes.tts: Dorsal is the side where the back and the neural plate will form. Ventral is the belly side.
scenes.visual: Dorsal and ventral arrows appear on the gastrula; a faint neural plate outline on the dorsal side.
scenes.narration: Dorsal is the side where the back and the neural plate will form. Ventral is the belly side.

scenes.tts: In the nineteen twenties, Hilde Mangold and Hans Spemann grafted an organizer into another embryo.
scenes.caption: In the 1920s, Hilde Mangold and Hans Spemann grafted an organizer into another embryo.
scenes.visual: Label: 1920s, Mangold and Spemann. An organizer piece is lifted from one embryo and placed into a second.
scenes.narration: In the 1920s, Hilde Mangold and Hans Spemann grafted an organizer into another embryo.

scenes.tts: The host formed a second body axis. The organizer could change what nearby ectoderm became.
scenes.visual: The host embryo grows two body axes side by side; the ectoderm near the graft turns from skin color to neural color.
scenes.narration: The host formed a second body axis. The organizer could change what nearby ectoderm became.

scenes.tts: For decades, the question was what positive signal the organizer sends to make ectoderm neural.
scenes.visual: A question mark travels from the organizer toward the ectoderm. Label: a positive neural signal?
scenes.narration: For decades, the question was what positive signal the organizer sends to make ectoderm neural.

scenes.tts: Now the dish. Cut out the animal cap and culture it alone in salt solution.
scenes.visual: The cap is cut from the blastula and dropped into a dish of salt solution. Label: animal-cap explant.
scenes.narration: Now the dish. Cut out the animal cap and culture it alone in salt solution.

scenes.tts: Left alone, what should a piece of skin-to-be become? Make a guess.
scenes.visual: The cap sits alone in the dish. Question on screen: alone, what does it become?
scenes.narration: Left alone, what should a piece of skin-to-be become? Make a guess.

scenes.tts: It becomes epidermis. No organizer tissue is attached to it.
scenes.visual: The cap flattens into a sheet of skin cells. Label: epidermis, the control. Note: no organizer tissue attached.
scenes.narration: It becomes epidermis. No organizer tissue is attached to it.

scenes.tts: One more pair of names. B M Ps, bone morphogenetic proteins, are secreted signals of the T G F beta family.
scenes.caption: One more pair of names. BMPs, bone morphogenetic proteins, are secreted signals of the TGF-beta family.
scenes.visual: A secreted protein dimer drifts out of a cell. Label: BMP, bone morphogenetic protein, TGF-beta family.
scenes.narration: One more pair of names. BMPs, bone morphogenetic proteins, are secreted signals of the TGF-beta family.

scenes.tts: Inside a cell, their signal is carried to the nucleus by Smad one, Smad five and Smad eight.
scenes.caption: Inside a cell, their signal is carried to the nucleus by Smad1, Smad5 and Smad8.
scenes.visual: Arrows run from the membrane to the nucleus; labels: Smad1, Smad5, Smad8.
scenes.narration: Inside a cell, their signal is carried to the nucleus by Smad1, Smad5 and Smad8.

scenes.tts: The map raises three puzzles. First, what holds an intact cap as skin?
scenes.visual: Three numbered boxes appear. Box 1: what holds an intact cap as skin?
scenes.narration: The map raises three puzzles. First, what holds an intact cap as skin?

scenes.tts: Second, what does the organizer send, and how does it change the ectoderm's fate?
scenes.visual: Box 2: what does the organizer send?
scenes.narration: Second, what does the organizer send, and how does it change the ectoderm's fate?

scenes.tts: Third, does the answer hold outside the frog cap: in the whole embryo, in a fly, in a chick?
scenes.visual: Box 3: does it hold in the embryo, a fly, a chick? Small icons of a frog embryo, a fly and a chick.
scenes.narration: Third, does the answer hold outside the frog cap: in the whole embryo, in a fly, in a chick?

scenes.tts: Here is the idea to carry through every chapter. B M P says skin. In early frog animal caps, turn its signal down far enough, and the cells become neural, as long as they can still respond and their other needed inputs, such as F G F, are intact.
scenes.caption: Here is the idea to carry through every chapter. BMP says skin. In early frog animal caps, turn its signal down far enough, and the cells become neural, as long as they can still respond and their other needed inputs, such as FGF, are intact.
scenes.visual: A single round dial labeled Smad1 in the nucleus, high (skin) at one end and low (neural) at the other, with three hands reaching for it: outside the cell, at the membrane, inside the cell. A separate arrow labeled FGF-dependent input feeds the neural side beside the dial. Text on screen: in early frog animal caps, BMP says skin; turn its signal down far enough and competent cells become neural, with other inputs such as FGF intact.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea to carry through every chapter. BMP says skin. In early frog animal caps, turn its signal down far enough, and the cells become neural, as long as they can still respond and their other needed inputs, such as FGF, are intact.

scenes.tts: B M P's effect comes down to one dial, Smad one activity in the nucleus. The next chapters show three hands that turn it down.
scenes.caption: BMP's effect comes down to one dial, Smad1 activity in the nucleus. The next chapters show three hands that turn it down.
scenes.visual: A single round dial labeled Smad1 in the nucleus, high (skin) at one end and low (neural) at the other, with three hands reaching for it: outside the cell, at the membrane, inside the cell. Small label under the dial: the BMP side of the decision. A separate arrow labeled FGF-dependent input feeds the same decision beside the dial.
scenes.narration: BMP's effect comes down to one dial, Smad1 activity in the nucleus. The next chapters show three hands that turn it down.
